newsitem.title: USA: Clinton goes to church on crutches.
newsitem.headline: Clinton goes to church on crutches.

text.p: President Clinton went to church on crutches on Sunday and took a mini-stroll at the White House as he sought some relief from the wheelchair he has used since knee surgery over a week ago.

The president took his longest public walk on crutches so far after the service, from the church door down about a half dozen steps to the van holding his wheelchair, with Secret Service men hovering at his elbows and church bells pealing.
Part of the way down the steps, Clinton used a hand railing and just one crutch. Parishioners of the Foundry United Methodist Church watched the scene anxiously.

Clinton usually attends the church when he is in town, and sat in the front row Sunday. Some in the congregation giggled when the pastor asked for prayer for those in the hospital "and in various stages of recovery."

Asked by a reporter outside the church how the crutches felt, Clinton smiled and said, "Better. Feels fine. Thanks." He then lowered himself into his wheelchair, which was sitting on a special elevator platform that was raised into the van.
However, the president ignored a question about whether he had made any telephone calls from the White House to raise money for his Democratic party.

Arriving back at the White House, Clinton did not go inside immediately but used the crutches for a little early spring stroll from his van to the Rose Garden, a journey of perhaps a couple of hundred feet.

White House officials said Clinton planned to spend the rest of the day in some "rigorous" physical therapy -- and watching basketball on television. His wife Hillary and daughter Chelsea were travelling in Africa.
Clinton's right knee was surgically repaired on March 14 after he tore a tendon by stumbling on some steps at the Florida estate of Australian golfer Greg Norman.

He left the hospital on March 16 and has been wheelchair-bound since then. The president restricted his activities to the White House until Wednesday evening, when he left town for a two-day summit in Helsinki, Finland with Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
